title: Probabilistic trip calibrator and context-preserving fallbacks
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Design and implement a probabilistic trip-point calibrator for per-entity (dependency/model/tenant) circuit breakers plus a context-preserving fallback proxy layer. Goal: replace coarse global trip thresholds with a statistically robust detector that reduces false-positive trips during benign spikes, while enabling safe degraded responses when a dependent model or region becomes unreliable.
acceptance_criteria: Per-entity breaker maintains Bayesian posterior over latency/error and only trips when posterior probability of SLO breach > configured alpha for N windows
Fallback proxy returns syntactically correct, context-preserving degraded responses (cached prefix + abbreviated continuation) 95% of requests when primary model is tripped
End-to-end canary run for a subset of tenants for 72 hours with <3% false-positive trips and without increased 95th percentile tail latency for non-affected tenants
Dashboard with per-entity trip-rate, posterior confidence, and simulated counterfactuals available in Console (runtime-1.22 release)
design_notes: Motivation: current threshold rules are brittle — global thresholds either overfit to noisy tenants or require per-tenant manual tuning. We need a model that adapts quickly but is statistically conservative.

Detector: maintain a small-window Bayesian model per entity that tracks interarrival/latency distributions and error rates. Use conjugate priors (Beta for errors, Normal-Inverse-Gamma for latency) for cheap updates in streaming fashion.

Trip logic: compute P(SLO violation | observations) over sliding windows (default windows: 1m, 5m, 15m). Trip if weighted aggregate posterior > alpha (default alpha=0.995) and minimum sample count reached.

Graceful soft-trip: when tripped, enter a staged degrade mode: (1) shadow-only diversion for 30s, (2) limited degraded responses (token-limited) with preserved context for 60s, (3) full reroute to fallback models if still failing.

Fallback semantics: preserve user prompt and KV prefix; synthesize a short, explicit degraded continuation using either cached recent completions or a smaller quantized model hosted in lower-cost pool. Responses must include metadata about reason and confidence to aid clients.
Per-tenant policy overrides: allow allowlist/denylist and strictness profiles (aggressive/conservative) in Dedicated and Private deployments.
Interaction with multi-region failover: breakers are local to region by default; we implement cross-region quorum checking for critical tenants before global reroute to avoid cascading failures.

Cost/Performance tradeoffs: Bayesian tracking adds ~8 bytes/entity and O(1) math per request; degraded responses may increase compute on fallback pool — cap degraded tokens per-request and per-tenant budget.
Security: fallback pool runs in same VPC/account for Private; no user data is sent to third-party services. Security review flagged KMS usage for metrics encryption at rest.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): prototype Bayesian detector in canary runtime - PR #6378 - 1 week
Phase 2 (engine): integrate detector into router, add per-entity state store (hot cache + RocksDB fallback), and implement staged soft-trip flow - 3 weeks
Phase 3 (fallback): build context-preserving degraded responder service (quantized small model + cached prefix store), integrate with token budget enforcement - 2 weeks
Phase 4 (observability): add Console panels (trip confidence, simulated SLO probability), tracing hooks and alert rules - 1 week
Phase 5 (canary): opt-in canary with 50 tenants in us-west-2/us-east-1 for 72 hours, measure false positives and recovery behaviors - 1 week
Phase 6 (rollout): staged ramp to 10% traffic, then 50%, then global with rollback knobs - 2 weeks
rollout_plan: Canary config: expose runtime flag 'breaker_v2' — default off. Enable for 50 non-critical tenants and internal test tenants.
Safeguards: immediate global kill switch, per-tenant dry-run mode where trips are logged but not enforced, rate-limited degraded responses, and strict token caps to prevent cost blowouts.
Monitoring: require green on canary metrics (false-positive rate <3%, SLOs for unaffected tenants unchanged) before increasing exposure.
Communication: notify Solutions and Support teams + update status page playbook with troubleshooting steps when breaker trips are observed.
Rollback: automatic rollback if client-facing error rate increases >1% absolute or median latency for remaining traffic increases >10% over baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert A1: Per-entity trip rate > 0.5% over a 5m window for 3 consecutive windows => Pager (oncall)
Alert A2: Canary false-positive rate > 3% over 1h => Slack/ops channel and block rollout
Dashboard D1: Trip confidence distribution heatmap (per-region, per-tenant, per-model)
Dashboard D2: Fallback success rate and median degraded-token usage
Logging: attach trip-reasons and posterior snapshots to traces for postmortem and simulation replay
testing_strategy: Unit: priors/posterior math and window aggregation determinism
Integration: router + breaker statestore + degraded responder in staging with synthetic spike generator
Chaos: simulated region outage where primary pool returns 5xx for 2 minutes to validate staged soft-trip and cross-region quorum behavior
Load: ensure breaker bookkeeping scales to 1M active entities with bounded memory growth
Safety: manual review of fallback response examples to avoid hallucinations; include policy to prepend a fixed disclaimer and result provenance.
